Name: Dash Flow
Keywords: flow; dataflow; traffic; request; arrow; connector; stream
Semantic Meaning: data is actively flowing between two connected services along this path
Stagger Rule: none, single continuous line
Performance Note: GPU-compositable; keep dasharray segment count low on paths over 500px to avoid jank
Reduced-Motion Fallback: solid stroke, no dash pattern, no offset animation
Do: use for connectors representing continuous data transfer
Don't: don't use on a connector representing a single one-time event, use connection-draw-in

Name: Packet Travel
Keywords: packet; message; request; travel; move; latency; unit
Semantic Meaning: a single discrete request or message unit is moving from sender to receiver right now
Stagger Rule: offset each concurrent packet's animation-delay by 150-300ms so packets do not overlap visually
Performance Note: cheap; offset-path runs on the compositor when only offset-distance is animated
Reduced-Motion Fallback: packet icon parked at the destination node, path drawn as a static solid line
Do: use for a single discrete message or request unit
Don't: don't use for aggregate/bulk continuous transfer, use stream-continuous instead

Name: Pulse Glow
Keywords: active; healthy; highlight; glow; status; node; alive; busy; processing; working; live
Semantic Meaning: this node is currently active, healthy, and processing work
Stagger Rule: none, or stagger by 200ms per node when highlighting a group simultaneously
Performance Note: drop-shadow is GPU-accelerated but costly at scale; limit to under 10 simultaneously pulsing nodes
Reduced-Motion Fallback: node rendered at full opacity with a fixed static glow, no pulsing
Do: use to mark a currently active, healthy, or processing node
Don't: don't use to represent an error state, use error-propagation or circuit-breaker-flicker instead

Name: Queue Fill
Keywords: queue; buffer; mq; depth; backlog; fill-level; capacity
Semantic Meaning: messages are accumulating in a buffer while waiting to be consumed
Stagger Rule: none
Performance Note: clip-path insets are compositor-friendly; avoid animating box-shadow alongside it
Reduced-Motion Fallback: bar rendered at its current fill level, no growth animation
Do: use for message queue, buffer, or bucket depth
Don't: don't use for binary on/off states, use pulse-glow or a plain opacity transition instead

Name: Round Trip
Keywords: request; response; latency; round-trip; rpc; api-call; rtt
Semantic Meaning: a request left this service and its response is coming back, showing round-trip latency
Stagger Rule: return-leg animation-delay equals outbound duration (e.g. 600ms) so the response starts after the request arrives
Performance Note: needs-js because hop count varies per scenario; keep to 4 or fewer hops to avoid jank; css-only form loops one token out-and-back; a JS version could vary hop count and fire on a real event
Reduced-Motion Fallback: both legs shown as static solid arrows, response arrow already at the origin
Do: use for request/response pairs to visualize latency
Don't: don't use for fire-and-forget async messages, use dash-flow or fanout-broadcast instead

Name: Retry Loop
Keywords: retry; backoff; failure; attempt; resilience; loop; exponential-backoff
Semantic Meaning: a failed call is being retried automatically after backoff; expect repeated attempts
Stagger Rule: each retry attempt is delayed by the previous attempt duration plus a backoff gap; JS computes attempt count
Performance Note: needs-js because attempt count is variable per scenario; cap rendered attempts at 3-5; css-only form widens gaps via calc backoff; a JS version could use the real attempt count and jitter
Reduced-Motion Fallback: single arrow shown looping back to the origin with a static retry-count badge
Do: use to show automatic retry-with-backoff behavior
Don't: don't use for a single manual retry, a plain connection-draw-in is enough

Name: Circuit Breaker Flicker
Keywords: circuit-breaker; cb; resilience; open-closed; failure; toggle; half-open
Semantic Meaning: the circuit breaker is toggling between closed and open state to protect a failing dependency
Stagger Rule: none
Performance Note: cheap; opacity and stroke-color swap only
Reduced-Motion Fallback: breaker shown in its current state color with no flicker
Do: use to show a breaker actively tripping between closed and open
Don't: don't use for a permanently open or closed breaker, use a static color instead

Name: Cache Hit Miss
Keywords: cache; hit; miss; lookup; redis; ttl; cdn
Semantic Meaning: a lookup just resolved from cache (hit) or fell through to the source of truth (miss)
Stagger Rule: none
Performance Note: cheap opacity flash only
Reduced-Motion Fallback: static hit or miss badge shown next to the cache node, no flash
Do: use immediately after a lookup to show hit vs miss outcome
Don't: don't use for ongoing cache warm-up, use batch-tick or stream-continuous instead

Name: Fanout Broadcast
Keywords: fanout; broadcast; pubsub; publish; subscriber; event-bus; topic; event; consumer; delivery; simultaneous
Semantic Meaning: one event was published and is being delivered to every subscriber simultaneously
Stagger Rule: each subscriber branch delayed 80-120ms in publish order; JS generates N branches per scenario
Performance Note: needs-js because subscriber count is scenario-variable; batch DOM writes for over 10 targets; css-only form needs one authored path per subscriber; a JS version could generate branches from a live list
Reduced-Motion Fallback: all branch lines drawn solid and fully visible at once
Do: use for pub/sub or event broadcast to multiple consumers
Don't: don't use for point-to-point request/response, use round-trip instead

Name: Backpressure
Keywords: backpressure; throttle; flow-control; congestion; rate; downstream; overload
Semantic Meaning: downstream is signaling it cannot keep up, so the flow rate is being throttled back
Stagger Rule: none
Performance Note: transform scaleX is compositor-friendly
Reduced-Motion Fallback: connector rendered narrowed to its throttled width, static
Do: use when downstream signals it cannot keep up with the inbound rate
Don't: don't use for a hard rejection, use load-shedding instead

Name: Heartbeat
Keywords: heartbeat; health-check; liveness; ping; monitor; alive; uptime
Semantic Meaning: this node is periodically confirming it is alive to a health monitor
Stagger Rule: none, or 300ms offset per node in a health-check group
Performance Note: transform scale is cheap and compositor-friendly
Reduced-Motion Fallback: node shown with a static heartbeat icon, no scaling
Do: use for periodic liveness or health-check signals
Don't: don't use for one-time boot confirmation, use node-boot-sequence instead

Name: Connection Draw-In
Keywords: connection; dependency; new-link; draw; onboarding; topology; link
Semantic Meaning: a new connection or dependency between two components was just established
Stagger Rule: none
Performance Note: stroke-dashoffset draw-in is compositor-friendly for paths under roughly 1000px
Reduced-Motion Fallback: connector rendered fully drawn, solid stroke
Do: use once when a new dependency or connection first appears in the diagram
Don't: don't use for a connector already part of the steady-state topology

Name: Node Boot Sequence
Keywords: boot; startup; initialization; sequence; deploy; order; bootstrap
Semantic Meaning: components are starting up in a defined order during system initialization
Stagger Rule: each subsequent node delayed by 400ms via nth-child(n) animation-delay of n times 0.4s
Performance Note: opacity fade-in only; cheap even for 10 or more nodes
Reduced-Motion Fallback: all nodes shown fully opaque and present, no sequential reveal
Do: use to show system startup or deployment order
Don't: don't use for a steady-state running system

Name: Error Propagation
Keywords: error; cascade; failure; propagation; cascade-ripple; dependency; outage
Semantic Meaning: a failure in one component is cascading to the components that depend on it
Stagger Rule: each downstream hop delayed 500ms from the failing node outward; covers the cascade-ripple alias
Performance Note: drop-shadow filter per node; limit propagation depth to 6 or fewer nodes for smoothness
Reduced-Motion Fallback: all affected nodes shown in the error color at once, no sequential reveal
Do: use to show a fault spreading through dependent services
Don't: don't use for an isolated single-node failure, use pulse-glow with the error color instead

Name: Load Shedding
Keywords: load-shedding; drop; overload; reject; throttle; 503; shed
Semantic Meaning: excess requests are being deliberately dropped to protect system stability
Stagger Rule: none
Performance Note: opacity plus transform fade; cheap
Reduced-Motion Fallback: dropped request shown as a static faded, crossed-out icon
Do: use to show requests deliberately rejected under overload
Don't: don't use for requests queued for later processing, use queue-fill instead

Name: Replication Sync
Keywords: replication; sync; replica; primary; consistency; geo-replication; followers
Semantic Meaning: data written to the primary is being copied to replica nodes to keep them consistent
Stagger Rule: each replica fade-in delayed 100-150ms in replication order; JS generates N replicas per topology
Performance Note: needs-js because replica count varies by topology; opacity-only animation keeps it cheap; css-only form needs one element per replica; a JS version could derive them from topology
Reduced-Motion Fallback: all replicas shown fully opaque and in sync, no fade sequence
Do: use to show data propagating from a primary to replica nodes
Don't: don't use for a one-off manual data copy, use dash-flow once instead

Name: Batch Tick
Keywords: batch; cron; scheduled; tick; interval; job; cron-job
Semantic Meaning: work is accumulating and will be processed together on the next scheduled interval
Stagger Rule: none
Performance Note: transform translateX with steps() is compositor-friendly
Reduced-Motion Fallback: batch counter shown at its current tick value, static
Do: use for scheduled or cron-driven batch processing intervals
Don't: don't use for continuous unbounded streams, use stream-continuous instead

Name: Stream Continuous
Keywords: stream; continuous; event-stream; kafka; tail; realtime; unbounded
Semantic Meaning: data is flowing continuously and indefinitely, not as discrete events
Stagger Rule: none
Performance Note: translate or background-position loop is cheap and compositor-friendly
Reduced-Motion Fallback: connector shown as a solid line with a static flow-direction arrow
Do: use for unbounded, always-on data streams such as event streams or log tailing
Don't: don't use for a bounded discrete transfer, use dash-flow or packet-travel instead

Name: Throttle Gate
Keywords: throttle; rate-limit; gate; admission; limiter; quota; lb
Semantic Meaning: requests above the allowed rate are being held back at a gate before entering the system
Stagger Rule: none
Performance Note: clip-path is compositor-friendly
Reduced-Motion Fallback: gate shown in its current open or closed width, static
Do: use to show a rate limiter admitting or blocking requests
Don't: don't use for total request rejection, use load-shedding instead

Name: Scale-Out Spawn
Keywords: autoscaling; scale-out; spawn; instance; k8s; horizontal-scaling; replica-set
Semantic Meaning: new instances are being created to handle increased load
Easing: var(--ease-spring-snappy) -- spring settle (damping ratio 0.6; one ~9.5% overshoot); plain ease-out where the token is absent
Stagger Rule: each new instance delayed 100-150ms in spawn order; JS generates N instances per scenario
Performance Note: needs-js because instance count is scenario-variable; opacity plus scale keeps each spawn cheap; css-only form needs one element per instance; a JS version could derive the count from the scenario
Reduced-Motion Fallback: all new instances shown fully present at final scale, no spawn sequence
Do: use to show autoscaling adding capacity under load
Don't: don't use for scale-down or termination, invert the keyframe direction instead

Name: Token Bucket Refill
Keywords: token-bucket; rate-limit; refill; quota; leaky-bucket; capacity; throttle
Semantic Meaning: capacity tokens are being replenished over time and consumed by incoming requests
Stagger Rule: none
Performance Note: opacity plus transform step animation; cheap
Reduced-Motion Fallback: bucket shown at its current token count, static tick marks
Do: use to visualize rate-limiting via token accumulation and consumption
Don't: don't use for hard throttling with no accumulation, use throttle-gate instead

Name: Leader Election Pulse
Keywords: leader-election; raft; paxos; consensus; quorum; primary; candidate
Semantic Meaning: nodes are voting and one candidate is becoming the new leader
Inline Snippet: .candidate{animation:elect 1s ease-in-out 2}.leader{animation:leaderglow 1.6s ease-in-out infinite}@keyframes elect{50%{opacity:.5}}@keyframes leaderglow{0%,100%{filter:drop-shadow(0 0 3px gold)}50%{filter:drop-shadow(0 0 10px gold)}}
Stagger Rule: candidate flicker plays twice, then the winning node switches to the continuous leader-glow loop
Performance Note: cheap opacity and filter animation; limit to the candidate set size, typically 3-5 nodes
Reduced-Motion Fallback: winning node shown with a static leader badge and glow, others shown as plain followers
Do: use for Raft or Paxos leader election, or primary promotion
Don't: don't use for routine heartbeats between an already-elected leader and followers, use heartbeat instead

Name: State Transition Arrow
Keywords: state-machine; fsm; transition; workflow; status; step; orchestration
Semantic Meaning: the system just moved from one defined state to another in response to an event
Stagger Rule: none
Performance Note: stroke-dashoffset plus color swap; cheap
Reduced-Motion Fallback: arrow shown fully drawn in the active-transition color, current state highlighted
Do: use to show a state machine or workflow moving between defined states
Don't: don't use for continuous flow with no discrete states, use stream-continuous instead

Name: Failover Reroute
Keywords: failover; reroute; standby; ha; split-brain; partition-split; redundancy
Semantic Meaning: traffic that was going to a failed node is being redirected to a healthy standby
Stagger Rule: new-path animation-delay equals old-path fade-out duration (400ms) so reroute starts after failure is visible
Performance Note: opacity plus stroke-dashoffset on two elements only; cheap
Reduced-Motion Fallback: failed path shown dimmed and crossed-out, new path shown solid and fully drawn
Do: use to show traffic switching from a failed node to a healthy standby; covers split-brain/partition-split framing
Don't: don't use for planned/manual traffic shifting, use dash-flow with a label instead

Name: Shard Distribute
Keywords: sharding; partition; consistent-hashing; shard; split-brain; partition-split; hash-ring
Semantic Meaning: data is being partitioned and routed to the specific shard that owns it
Stagger Rule: each shard's animation-delay staggered by 100ms in shard-key order; JS generates N shard paths
Performance Note: needs-js because shard count is scenario-variable; offset-path per shard target
Reduced-Motion Fallback: each data row shown already parked at its owning shard, no travel animation
Do: use to show consistent-hashing or range-based data partitioning; covers split-brain/partition-split framing
Don't: don't use for simple replication, use replication-sync instead

Name: TTL Expiry
Keywords: ttl; expiry; cache-eviction; session; expire; lifecycle; timeout
Semantic Meaning: a cached or session item has reached its time-to-live limit and is being evicted
Stagger Rule: none
Performance Note: opacity plus transform scale on a single element; cheap
Reduced-Motion Fallback: expired item shown removed or greyed-out immediately, no fade sequence
Do: use to show a cache entry or session reaching its time-to-live limit
Don't: don't use for manual/explicit eviction, use load-shedding or a plain fade instead

Name: Camera Beat
Keywords: camera; zoom; beat; storyboard; focus; narrative; cinematic; walkthrough; tour; pan; act; chapter
Semantic Meaning: the diagram tells its story in timed acts: the camera zooms to one area, explains it with a caption or an interior detail view, then returns to the full overview
Duration: one master timeline; each beat a multiple of the diagram's ambient beat (e.g. 4800ms), zoom moves 600ms
Easing: ease-in-out on the move segments, linear master
Stagger Rule: beats are sequential slices of one master duration; captions and morph layers key off the same percentages
Performance Note: one transform on a single wrapper group runs on the compositor; never animate viewBox (needs JS and re-layouts every frame)
Reduced-Motion Fallback: camera parked at the full overview (the final beat), captions hidden, every ambient motion at its own end state; the svg desc carries the narration
Do: use to walk a viewer through a system in a fixed order, and for short-video exports where beats become chapters
Don't: don't add scroll, click, or hover control -- beats auto-play on an infinite loop (locked product decision); don't zoom so far that off-screen context loses meaning

Name: State Timeline
Keywords: staged failure; domino; cascade failure; node dies; load rises; scenario; degrade over time; staged state; act; overload
Semantic Meaning: a component's condition CHANGES over the story -- healthy, then overloaded, then down, then the failure cascades to its neighbours -- with every transition keyed to the master timeline
Duration: windows are percentages of the master, not absolute ms; each transition window is a divisor-true fraction of it (16% of a 24s master = 3840ms)
Easing: linear on the master; ~0.6s crossfade at each window edge
Stagger Rule: domino onsets are ordered -- each downstream stage's window opens after the upstream one's, spaced by that edge's propagation time from the sheet's event table
Performance Note: opacity on one overlay group per stage; the base node is never repainted, so every stage stays on the compositor
Reduced-Motion Fallback: the story's end state shown statically -- final act only, each component resting in its last condition with its chip visible; never a frozen mid-cascade montage
Do: stage OVERLAYS (dashed ring, chip, fill-bar from states.csv + state-effects.css) whose opacity carries a data-window on the master; keep every transition's caption claim on the sheet's event table
Don't: never mutate the base node's paint properties (stroke-dasharray, stroke, fill) -- those animate off-compositor; a staged state is an overlay group whose OPACITY carries the window, same law as the beat spotlight

Name: Shake Stress
Keywords: shake; tremble; stress; strain; judder; rattle; vibrate; straining; under load; at capacity
Semantic Meaning: this component is visibly trembling under a load it cannot absorb -- the educational register's intensity for is-overloaded
Duration: 120ms per tremble (90-120ms is the legible band); under a master timeline pick a divisor -- 120ms divides a 38.4s master 320 times
Stagger Rule: none -- one component trembles at a time; if two shake in the same window offset one by half a cycle so they do not read as mechanically linked
Performance Note: transform on the state overlay or a body group only; the 1.5px amplitude keeps the node's own label legible and the layer stays on the compositor
Reduced-Motion Fallback: no shake -- the fill-level bar and the numeric chip carry the overload on their own
Do: use inside an is-overloaded data-window to give the educational register its intensity; shake the overlay/body group and pair it with the chip that carries the number
Don't: never shake a dead node -- stillness is death's meaning; never displace more than 2px, past that the label stops being readable

Name: Collapse Death
Keywords: collapse; death; dying moment; buckle; crumple; keel over; flatline; one-shot; gives out
Semantic Meaning: the dying MOMENT: the node buckles once as it goes down, then stays permanently still
Duration: 480ms, once, at the START of the is-down window; under a master timeline pick a divisor -- 480ms divides a 38.4s master 80 times
Stagger Rule: in a domino each victim's collapse starts at its own is-down onset, spaced by that edge's propagation time from the sheet's event table
Performance Note: one transform on the node body inside the window; forwards fill holds the settled pose, so the rest of the window costs nothing
Reduced-Motion Fallback: no collapse -- the is-down static encoding (sparse dash, 40% fill, error stroke, DOWN chip) is the resting truth
Do: play it ONCE at the start of an is-down window with forwards fill; everything after it is the static dead state
Don't: never loop the collapse -- a node cannot die twice; never animate paint (fill/stroke) alongside it, that takes the node off the compositor
